column5: Reading the word BLUE printed in red ink slows color naming, the classic interference named for this psychologist.
A witness who later hears misleading details may incorporate them into a recollection, an effect extensively studied by Elizabeth Loftus.
People may miss a gorilla crossing a basketball-passing scene when their attention is occupied by counting passes.
An upside-down face can conceal grotesquely reversed eyes and mouth that become obvious when the image is upright, a named illusion created with a British prime minister's portrait.
In recall, items from the beginning and end of a list usually outperform those from its middle.
Taking practice quizzes strengthens later recall more than simply rereading the same material, a benefit known by this name.
An individual may pull less hard on a rope when tugging as part of a team than when tugging alone.
After discussion, like-minded group members often shift toward a more extreme version of their original position.
A crowd of witnesses can make each person feel less personally obligated to help because responsibility seems spread among all present.
Success credited to one's talent but failure blamed on bad luck displays this self-protective attribution pattern.
A person may cling to an initial belief even after the evidence that created it has been completely discredited.
After learning an outcome, people commonly overestimate how predictable it had seemed beforehand.
People often treat one offered serving as the proper amount, whether the scoop or package is small or large, illustrating this bias.
Remembering that a dentist appointment must be kept tomorrow uses this future-oriented form of memory.
Knowing a fact while forgetting whether it came from a professor, podcast, or rumor is this source-related memory error.
After deprivation of dream-rich sleep, people often spend an unusually large proportion of later sleep in that stage.
This researcher's retention studies produced a curve showing that memory loss is initially steep and then levels off.
Unfinished tasks remaining more mentally accessible than completed ones bear the name of this Soviet psychologist.
A distinctive item, such as the only red word in a black list, receives a memory advantage named for this German psychiatrist.
Craik and Lockhart proposed that durable memory depends more on semantic analysis than on shallow visual processing in this framework.
In Baddeley's working-memory architecture, this component briefly maintains speech-based information through rehearsal.
Mental rotation and remembering a route draw on this visual-spatial component of working memory.
This supervisory part of Baddeley's model allocates attention and coordinates its specialized temporary stores.
People often overestimate how widely others share their own opinions and preferences.
We tend to explain another person's behavior dispositionally but our own similar behavior situationally, a contrast with this name.
Belief that people generally get what they deserve can lead observers to blame an innocent victim.
Garcia's rats readily linked nausea with taste but not with a light, evidence that organisms are biologically ready to learn some associations.
Rewarding an enjoyable activity can sometimes reduce later voluntary interest in it once the reward disappears.
Walter Mischel's preschool study used a marshmallow to examine children's capacity for this form of self-control.
Wolpe paired gradual exposure to feared stimuli with relaxation in this behavioral treatment.
A classroom may award points exchangeable for privileges, applying this contingency-based behavior system.
Judgments of sensation depend on separating sensory sensitivity from willingness to say yes, the central idea of this theory.
The barely detectable gap separating two weights grows in proportion to the starting weight under this psychophysical regularity.
Perceived magnitude often follows physical intensity raised to an exponent, a relation named for this Harvard psychophysicist.
After staring at a green image, a red afterimage supports this account in which paired color channels inhibit one another.
Treisman proposed that focused attention binds separately processed color, shape, and orientation using this model.
On this influential view, perception continually compares top-down expectations with incoming sensory errors.
In semantic networks, thinking of doctor can hasten recognition of nurse because activation travels among related concepts.
Tulving and Thomson argued that retrieval succeeds when cues present at recall overlap those encoded with the event.
column6: What is the encoding specificity principle?

column5: Memory improves when the mental operations used at study resemble those required by the final test, according to this principle.
A retrieved memory can briefly become labile and require restabilization, a process exploited in some fear studies.
Preexposure to a harmless tone can slow later conditioning of that tone with shock.
Once one cue already predicts an outcome, a second cue added beside it may acquire little associative strength.
This learning model updates a cue most when the outcome differs from expectation, formalizing prediction error.
Performance often peaks at an intermediate arousal level, with harder tasks favoring lower arousal, under this named relationship.
Bem argued that when internal cues are weak, people may infer their attitudes by observing their own actions.
Petty and Cacioppo's persuasion model contrasts careful argument scrutiny with reliance on surface cues.
column6: What is the elaboration likelihood model?

column5: A small initial request can increase compliance with a larger related request later, this aptly named technique.
Old information disrupting acquisition of new material, as when a former password intrudes on learning a replacement, is this.
New learning impairing recall of older material, such as Italian lessons disrupting remembered Spanish, is this complementary effect.
Two targets appearing rapidly in one stream can make detection of the first briefly impair detection of the second.
Two rapidly required responses interfere because a central processing stage cannot select both at once, producing this bottleneck.
column6: What is the psychological refractory period?

column5: Judging Linda more likely to be both a bank teller and feminist than merely a bank teller commits this probability error.
Ignoring the prevalence of a disease while focusing on an impressive diagnostic description exemplifies this reasoning error.
A price described as 90 percent survival can seem preferable to one described as 10 percent mortality because of this effect.
Ownership alone can make a mug seem worth more to its seller than to an otherwise identical prospective buyer.
Preference for a smaller reward now over a larger delayed reward often falls steeply at first and then more slowly under this model.
Higgins distinguished striving toward gains from guarding against losses in this account of promotion and prevention orientations.
Salience of mortality can intensify defense of cultural worldviews, according to this social-psychological account.
Tajfel's minimal-group studies support this theory that group memberships help organize the self-concept.
Concern about confirming a negative group belief can itself impair performance, a phenomenon demonstrated by Steele and Aronson.
Deci and Ryan's motivation theory centers autonomy, competence, and relatedness as basic psychological needs.
Sweller's instructional account separates intrinsic demands from avoidable demands imposed by poor presentation.
Damage to visual cortex can leave patients reporting no visual awareness while guessing stimulus locations above chance.
Reaction time increases with the logarithm of the number of response alternatives under this information-theoretic decision law.
This sequential-sampling model treats a two-choice decision as noisy evidence accumulating until one boundary is reached.
In this consciousness theory, information becomes reportable when broadcast widely across a network of specialized processors.
column6: What is global neuronal workspace theory?

column5: A psychometric test's expected reliability after changing its length can be estimated with this named formula.
column6: What is the Spearman-Brown prophecy formula?

column5: This family of psychometric models estimates an item's difficulty and discrimination separately from a person's latent ability.
A model with separate fast familiarity and slower recollection processes offers this kind of account of recognition memory.
column6: What is a dual-process model of recognition?

column5: The tendency for generalization responses to peak away from the trained cue after discrimination learning bears this name.
A weak conditioned response to one stimulus because a more salient companion dominated learning illustrates this cue-competition effect.
A cue that signals omission of an otherwise expected outcome acquires this inhibitory associative role.
A stimulus that tells an animal when another cue-outcome relation is in force serves this modulatory function.
Under Herrnstein's quantitative law, relative response rates track relative reinforcement rates across concurrent choices.
This principle says a more probable behavior can reinforce a less probable one, as playtime might reward finishing homework.
Intermittently rewarded behavior can resist extinction more than continuously rewarded behavior, a paradoxical result called this.
column6: What is the partial-reinforcement extinction effect?

column5: In prospect theory, people often overweight outcomes that are guaranteed relative to outcomes that are merely probable, an asymmetry called this.
Failing to recognize one side of space after right parietal damage is this attentional syndrome rather than an eye disorder.
A patient who recognizes a face yet insists the familiar person is an impostor exhibits this delusional misidentification syndrome.

column1: # Genetics: inheritance patterns, experimental history, molecular regulation, repair, and population processes.

column5: Crossing an individual of unknown dominant genotype with a homozygous recessive individual reveals the unknown genotype through offspring ratios.
Breeders may repeat a mating with the sexes reversed to test whether a trait's transmission depends on which parent carries it.
Yellow-coated mice crossed together yield a two-to-one ratio among living offspring because inheriting two copies has this consequence.
In Labrador retrievers, one locus can prevent pigment deposition and thereby mask the effect of a separate coat-color locus, specifically this recessive interaction.
A trait appears only after an underlying liability produced by genes and environment passes a critical level in this model.
Not every person carrying a disease-causing genotype shows the phenotype; this term describes the proportion who do.
People with the same genotype can show different degrees of a trait, variation described by this term.
Two linked dominant alleles on the same homolog, with both recessive alleles on the other, form an arrangement with this name.
The percentage of recombinant offspring can estimate distance between loci and is called this measurement.
Failure of homologs or sister chromatids to separate properly can produce gametes with extra or missing chromosomes.
In many mammalian female cells, a condensed inactive X chromosome appears microscopically as this structure.
The visible X-shaped contact between homologous chromosomes marks a site where reciprocal exchange has occurred.
Random orientation of homologous pairs at meiosis I underlies Mendel's law bearing this name.
An allele's expression can depend on whether it came from the mother or father because of parent-specific epigenetic marks.
A trait passed by an affected mother to children of both sexes, but not by an affected father, often follows this extranuclear pattern.
An organism containing cell populations with different genotypes descended from one zygote displays this condition.
White-eyed flies helped this Columbia researcher show that genes occupy chromosomes and that some traits are sex-linked.
Studying mealworm chromosomes, this scientist independently helped identify X and Y as determinants of sex.
The hypothesis that one X chromosome is randomly silenced in female mammals bears this British geneticist's name.
As an undergraduate in Morgan's fly lab, he drew the first linkage map by ordering genes from recombination rates.
This physician connected alkaptonuria to inherited metabolic chemistry and proposed the idea of inborn errors of metabolism.
Bread mold mutants led these two scientists to the one gene-one enzyme hypothesis.
column6: Who were George Beadle and Edward Tatum?

column5: Radioactive phosphorus entered bacteria while radioactive sulfur largely stayed with phage coats in this blender-assisted experiment.
Heavy nitrogen and density-gradient centrifugation revealed that each daughter DNA molecule contains one old strand and one new strand in this experiment.
Across species, the amount of adenine roughly equals thymine and guanine roughly equals cytosine under these empirical relationships.
Short pieces made on the lagging strand bear the name of the Japanese scientists who discovered them.
This ribonucleoprotein enzyme extends chromosome ends using an RNA template carried within itself.
Bacterial enzymes that cut DNA at particular recognition sequences became indispensable tools of molecular cloning.
DNA fragments migrate through a porous matrix at rates related to size during this standard separation method.
Chain-terminating dideoxynucleotides are the signature reagents of this classic DNA-reading method.
Repeated heating, primer annealing, and polymerase extension amplify a chosen DNA region in this technique.
A fluorescent or radioactive complementary nucleic-acid strand used to find a matching sequence is known by this term.
In E. coli, lactose availability and glucose scarcity activate this classic gene-regulatory unit studied by Jacob and Monod.
Abundant tryptophan makes a corepressor activate the repressor of this biosynthetic bacterial operon.
Placed between a regulatory element and a promoter, this boundary sequence can block their communication and can also separate chromatin domains.
A regulatory DNA element that recruits repressors to reduce transcription is called this.
Selecting different combinations of exons from one pre-mRNA allows a single gene to produce multiple protein isoforms.
Small RNAs provide sequence specificity to this Argonaute-containing complex, which silences complementary messenger RNA.
column6: What is the RNA-induced silencing complex?

column5: A messenger RNA lacking a termination codon can strand a ribosome at its 3-prime end and trigger this quality-control pathway.
Adding methyl groups to cytosines in CpG-rich promoters is commonly associated with reduced transcription.
Adding acetyl groups to lysines on histone tails often loosens chromatin and correlates with active transcription.
ATP-dependent protein complexes slide, eject, or restructure nucleosomes in this form of gene regulation.
LINEs and SINEs are mobile sequences that can copy themselves to new genomic locations and belong to this broad class.
Some bacteria can take up naked DNA directly from their surroundings through this mode of gene acquisition.
During recombination, nonreciprocal sequence copying can change one allele to match its homolog.
This scaled statistic, often written D with a prime mark, measures nonrandom association between alleles while accounting for the largest possible disequilibrium.
A marker allele co-inherited with a disease across a family can help locate the responsible region through this strategy.
Comparing affected and unaffected people at hundreds of thousands of variants is the basis of this population study design.
column6: What is a genome-wide association study?

column5: Four DNA strands meet in this cross-shaped recombination intermediate proposed in 1964.
This zipper-like protein structure holds homologous chromosomes together during meiotic prophase I.
This chromosome-maintenance complex containing two SMC proteins helps manage recombination intermediates and preserve genome stability.
During S phase, this protein stabilizes sister-chromatid cohesion by opposing the ring-releasing activity of WAPL.
This meiotic enzyme deliberately creates double-strand DNA breaks that initiate recombination.
Replication errors that escape proofreading are corrected when MutS-like proteins recognize distorted base pairing in this pathway.
UV-induced thymine dimers are removed as part of a short damaged oligonucleotide in this versatile repair pathway.
A DNA glycosylase starts this repair pathway by removing a chemically altered base while leaving the sugar-phosphate backbone.
Ku proteins bind broken chromosome ends before direct ligation in this error-prone double-strand break pathway.
Using an intact sister chromatid as a template allows accurate repair of a double-strand break by this mechanism.
A programmable nuclease made by fusing a FokI cutting domain to customizable DNA-binding motifs uses these finger-like modules.
These engineered nucleases join FokI to repeat arrays derived from bacterial transcription activator-like effectors.
Two short recognition sites flank DNA that can be excised or inverted by a phage-derived recombinase in this system.
An RNA molecule supplies the sequence specificity that directs a CRISPR-associated nuclease to its DNA target.
This short motif immediately beside a target is required for many CRISPR nucleases to distinguish suitable DNA.
column6: What is a protospacer adjacent motif?

column5: Introducing a designed nucleotide change without a double-strand break can use a Cas nickase fused to a deaminase in this method.
Parallel bacterial cultures produced wildly different numbers of resistant mutants, showing mutations arise before selection in this classic test.
column6: What is the Luria-Delbruck fluctuation experiment?

column5: Colonies copied from one plate to another retained the same resistant positions, demonstrating that resistance mutations predated exposure.
Two recessive mutations producing a normal phenotype when placed together in one cell are inferred to affect different genes by this test.
Recombination among bacteriophage T4 mutants let Seymour Benzer map mutation sites within a gene at extraordinary resolution using this experimental system.
Population subdivision can create an overall deficit of heterozygotes even when each subpopulation is individually in equilibrium, an effect named for this scientist.
With both recombination and ancestry represented, this graph generalizes a single gene tree by allowing different genomic segments to have different genealogies.
column6: What is an ancestral recombination graph?

column5: Molecular changes with no fitness effect can become fixed by drift under Motoo Kimura's influential evolutionary account.
column6: What is the neutral theory of molecular evolution?

column5: Selection at linked loci can reduce the effectiveness of selection in finite populations through this interference named for two geneticists.
In an asexual population, irreversible loss of the least-mutated class can drive accumulation of harmful variants in this ratchet-like process.
If only one hybrid sex is sterile or absent, this rule predicts that it is usually the heterogametic sex.
Alleles that work in their native populations can interact badly in hybrids, a speciation mechanism named for two evolutionary geneticists.
Asymmetric female meiosis can let stronger centromeres preferentially enter the egg rather than a polar body, a biased process called this.
Inheritance of both homologs of a chromosome pair from one parent rather than one from each is called this.
A tumor cell that began with one normal and one mutant allele may lose the remaining normal copy through this event.
Earlier onset or increasing severity across generations, often caused by expanding repeats, is described by this inheritance phenomenon.
Expansions of CAG or other three-base units cause disorders such as Huntington disease through this mutation class.
column6: What is a trinucleotide repeat expansion?

column1: # Periodic Table: historical development, periodic trends, chemical behavior, discovery, and naming.

column5: Aluminium, gallium, indium, tin, thallium, lead, and bismuth are often assigned this informal metal class lying beyond the transition elements.
Half the internuclear distance between two identical bonded atoms defines this experimentally useful size measure.
The ease with which an atom's electron cloud can be distorted generally increases down a group and is measured by this property.
Chemists using a thermodynamic sign convention call the enthalpy change when a gaseous atom accepts an electron this.
Differences in bond energies underpin this dimensionless ranking of atoms' attraction for shared electrons.
This tendency to lose electrons and form positive ions generally strengthens toward the lower-left corner of the table.
Dots placed around an element abbreviation represent its outer electrons in this compact bonding notation.
A eutectic mixture of sodium and potassium remains liquid near room temperature and is known by this blended formula-name.
Compounds such as magnesium bromide and calcium hydride contain a metal from group 2, whose two outer electrons occupy this block.
Compounds in which a group-15 element acts as the more negative partner, such as gallium arsenide, belong to this binary class.
Sulfides, selenides, and tellurides are grouped under this family name for binary compounds.
ClF3 and BrF5 combine two different salt-forming elements and therefore belong to this molecular class.
Neil Bartlett's reaction of xenon with platinum hexafluoride overturned the assumption of total inertness by producing the first recognized example of this class.
Absorption of visible light while an electron moves between split d orbitals helps give many central-block compounds their colors.
The two detached rows are collectively given this name because electrons progressively enter f orbitals.
Linear cations such as UO2 with a two-plus charge exemplify this dioxo structural family characteristic of several heavy 5f elements.
The Sanskrit prefix meaning one let Mendeleev label predicted placeholders such as the ones below boron and silicon using this system.
Independently of Mendeleev, this German chemist plotted atomic volume against atomic weight and developed a similar classification.
X-ray frequencies let this English physicist reorder elements by nuclear charge rather than atomic weight.
This Berkeley chemist proposed moving the 5f series below the main body, the arrangement now used for heavy elements.
Noticing that every eighth element repeated properties when ordered by weight, this chemist compared the pattern to music.
This German chemist grouped elements such as chlorine, bromine, and iodine in threes whose middle weight approximated the average of the other two.
De Chancourtois wrapped elements around a cylinder in this helical 1862 arrangement named for Earth.
A meeting held in this German city in 1860 helped standardize atomic weights after Cannizzaro distributed his ideas.
Violet spectral lines revealed the metal that matched eka-aluminium to this French discoverer in 1875.
column6: Who was Paul-Emile Lecoq de Boisbaudran?

column5: The predicted eka-silicon closely matched this element Clemens Winkler isolated from argyrodite.
Mendeleev's eka-boron prediction was vindicated by discovery of this element in Scandinavian minerals.
Discovery of argon and its unreactive relatives required adding an entirely new column bearing this historical number.
Mendeleev sometimes reversed neighboring elements, notably tellurium and iodine, rather than violate this more important criterion.
Seaborg recognized that thorium through lawrencium primarily fill this subshell, justifying their detached placement.
Bombarding uranium with neutrons led these two Berkeley researchers to identify neptunium, the first element beyond uranium.
column6: Who were Edwin McMillan and Philip Abelson?

column5: A temporary systematic name such as ununpentium was constructed digit by digit under this organization's nomenclature.
column6: What is the IUPAC systematic element naming scheme?

column5: In a simplified main-group model, subtracting core electrons from proton count gives this attraction felt by the outer shell.
An orbital's number of radial nodes equals n minus l minus one; at each such location its radial probability falls to zero.
An s electron samples density nearer the nucleus than a p electron in the same shell, giving it more of this orbital property.
Because 4f electrons screen poorly, this element at the series end is much more compact than a simple shell-count prediction suggests.
Lithium resembles magnesium, and beryllium resembles aluminium, across adjacent periods because of this slanting periodic relationship.
Heavier p-block elements may favor oxidation states two units below the group maximum because their ns pair resists bonding.
Very heavy atoms require this correction because inner electrons moving near light speed alter orbital sizes and energies.
Gold's yellow color and mercury's low melting point are both strongly influenced by contraction of this orbital type.
Chromium favors a 3d5 4s1 ground state partly because this arrangement gives extra stability to its d subshell.
Copper favors 3d10 4s1 partly because this completely occupied subshell has enhanced stability.
column6: What is a filled d subshell?

column5: Across a set of ions with equal electron counts, the species with more protons generally has the smaller radius; such a set is called this.
Aluminium oxide reacts with both acids and bases, exemplifying this dual acid-base behavior.
A thin adherent oxide layer makes aluminium and chromium much less reactive than their reduction potentials might suggest.
Carbon's exceptional ability to form long chains and rings by bonding to itself is this property.
White, red, and black phosphorus are structurally different forms of one element described by this phenomenon.
Combining species in high and low oxidation states to form an intermediate state, as iron metal and ferric ion form ferrous ion, is this reverse process.
Four elements take names from this Swedish village, whose quarry yielded minerals containing yttrium and several rare earths.
The celestial body commemorated by cerium had been found in 1801 by this astronomer at Palermo Observatory.
Palladium honors this asteroid, whose own name came from an epithet of Athena.
This woman proposed the name of element 61 from the myth of stolen fire; her husband Charles was on its discovery team.
Hafnium's name derives from Hafnia, the Latin name of this capital where it was discovered.
Rhenium takes its name directly from this Latin word for the great river of western Germany.
The name of lutetium preserves this Roman-era name for the settlement that became the French capital.
Ruthenium's name uses a Latin designation for this country, homeland of one discoverer.
Nihonium derives from a Japanese word meaning this country, where the element was first synthesized.
Darmstadtium honors the German city containing this heavy-ion research center, where the element was produced.
column6: What is GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research?

column5: Tennessine recognizes contributions from laboratories and researchers in this U.S. state.
Oganesson honors this nuclear physicist, one of the few people to have an element named for him while alive.
Samarium's name ultimately traces through a mineral to this Russian mining official, an early person indirectly honored by an element.
Hassium uses this Latin name for the German state containing Darmstadt, where the element was produced.
In 1900, this German physicist detected a radioactive gas emitted by radium; the gas was later named radon.
Gadolinium honors this Finnish chemist who isolated an oxide from the Ytterby mineral later called gadolinite.
These empirical screening rules estimate the net nuclear charge experienced by an electron from its configuration.
This electronegativity definition averages an atom's ionization energy and electron affinity.
This scale estimates attraction for bonding electrons from effective nuclear charge divided by the square of covalent radius.
The orbital-order mnemonic based on increasing n plus l, breaking ties by lower n, bears this name.
Soft acids favor soft bases and hard acids favor hard bases under this qualitative framework introduced by Pearson.
Small, highly charged cations tend to polarize large anions and increase covalent character under these rules.
Closed-shell gold(I) centers can attract one another at distances comparable to hydrogen bonds through this relativistically enhanced interaction.
Compounds containing polyanionic frameworks and electropositive counterions, often formed by post-transition elements, belong to this class named for a German chemist.
Electron concentration helps predict the stable structures of certain metallic alloys under these metallurgical rules.
The extra stability associated with parallel-spin electrons in degenerate orbitals is often described as this quantum contribution.
Successive filling of 5f orbitals produces a gradual size decrease across the heavy inner-transition series called this.
Subtle oscillations in rare-earth complex stability across the series are known collectively by this fourfold-sounding name.
column6: What is the lanthanide tetrad effect?

column5: A predicted region where certain superheavy nuclei have unusually long half-lives because of closed nuclear shells bears this geographic metaphor.
column6: What is the island of stability?

column5: Elements heavier than fermium are sometimes grouped under this collective term, especially in nuclear-chemistry history.
Cosmic and terrestrial abundances generally favor even-proton elements over adjacent odd-proton elements under this empirical rule.
In Pettifor's ordering, elements receive values on this empirical scale designed to organize structural chemistry beyond atomic number.

column1: # Energy & Forces: mechanics, gravitation, fields, fluids, elasticity, and variational principles.

column5: Rocket engineers divide thrust by propellant weight-flow rate to obtain this performance measure, commonly reported in seconds.
An electric traction motor used as a generator can slow a vehicle while sending its output into resistor banks as heat through this method.
With only conservative forces acting, the combined kinetic and potential forms remain constant under this principle.
column6: What is conservation of mechanical energy?

column5: Before two surfaces begin sliding, this contact force adjusts up to a maximum value to oppose impending motion.
At low Reynolds number, drag on a small sphere is proportional to viscosity, radius, and speed under this relation.
For uniform circular motion, the acceleration points toward the circle's center even when speed is constant.
The perpendicular distance from a rotation axis to a force's line of action is this rotational distance.
A blow delivered at this point on a bat or racket causes no impulsive reaction at the pivot, helping define its mechanical sweet spot.
column6: What is the center of percussion?

column5: A spring's displacement per unit applied force is this flexibility measure, the reciprocal of stiffness.
The negative ratio of transverse strain to axial strain describes how much a stretched material narrows.
James Watt popularized this unit equal to 550 foot-pounds per second while marketing steam engines.
Multiple pulleys sharing a rope form this rig, multiplying lifting force at the cost of pulling more rope.
column6: What is a block and tackle?

column5: This floating instrument sinks deeper in a less dense liquid and directly measures relative density.
A small piston driving a larger one lets this device multiply force through fluid pressure.
Flow speeds up and static pressure falls as fluid passes through a pipe constriction in this named effect.
Heat pumps may deliver more heating energy than their electrical input; output heat divided by work gives this ratio.
column6: What is the coefficient of performance?

column5: A spherically symmetric body attracts an external object as though all its mass were concentrated at its center under this result.
A torsion balance and lead spheres let this scientist determine Earth's density and effectively measure the gravitational constant.
Two hanging masses connected over a pulley form this apparatus for studying constant acceleration and Newton's second law.
Travel eastward on a rotating Earth slightly reduces apparent weight while westward travel increases it through this named effect.
The slow rotation of a long pendulum's swing plane provides a direct terrestrial demonstration that Earth turns.
A spinning wheel under gravity can turn its axis around the vertical rather than simply topple, exhibiting this motion.
The distance at which all a body's mass could be imagined concentrated to reproduce its rotational inertia is this quantity.
A heavy rotating disk smooths engine speed by storing rotational energy between power strokes.
This theorem shifts rotational inertia from a center-of-mass axis to another one by adding mass times the squared separation.
Relative speed of separation divided by relative speed of approach defines this collision parameter.
column6: What is the coefficient of restitution?

column5: A force field expressible as the negative gradient of a scalar has zero value for this line integral around any closed path.
Every point on one of these surfaces has the same potential, so moving along it requires no work from the associated field.
This orbital equation relates speed at any point to the central body's mass, current distance, and semimajor axis.
For an inverse-square gravitational orbit, negative total mechanical energy identifies this kind of trajectory.
A top's resistance to rapid changes of its spin axis is commonly described by this stabilizing behavior.
A rotating frame whose angular speed is itself changing introduces this tangential inertial effect, proportional to angular acceleration.
Subtracting potential energy from kinetic energy produces this function at the heart of one formulation of classical mechanics.
A physical path makes the action stationary relative to nearby possible paths under this variational rule.
If a Lagrangian has no explicit dependence on time, this first-integral identity yields a conserved energy-like quantity.
In canonical mechanics, this energy-like function generates time evolution of coordinates and momenta.
Angles, lengths, or other independent variables chosen to specify a constrained system are known by this term.
For an equilibrium system, imagined infinitesimal displacements compatible with constraints make the total of these imagined works vanish.
column6: What is the principle of virtual work?

column5: Adding inertial forces to applied forces turns a dynamics problem into a formal equilibrium statement under this principle.
If a Lagrangian does not depend explicitly on one generalized coordinate, that variable has this name and its conjugate momentum is conserved.
A force directed along the line joining a particle to a fixed point has this symmetry, guaranteeing angular-momentum conservation.
Combining an ordinary potential with an angular-momentum barrier reduces radial orbital motion to one dimension using this constructed function.
A two-body problem can be recast as one fictitious particle whose mass equals the product divided by the sum.
The second time derivative of a system's scalar moment of inertia can be expressed in terms of kinetic energy and force virial by this identity.
This conserved vector in the Kepler problem points toward periapsis and helps explain closed elliptical orbits.
The closed, nondegenerate two-form underlying canonical mechanics is this geometric structure.
All possible generalized positions, without their momenta, make up this lower-dimensional space.
Hamiltonian flow preserves volume in phase space under this theorem.
Locally, a uniformly accelerating laboratory is indistinguishable from a uniform gravitational field under Einstein's foundational idea.
A freely falling body follows this locally straightest possible path through curved spacetime.
Energy density, momentum density, pressure, and shear act as spacetime curvature's source through this rank-two object.
A rotating mass drags nearby inertial frames, an effect measured around Earth by Gravity Probe B.
Light climbing away from a massive body is observed at longer wavelengths through this general-relativistic effect.
Differences in gravity across an extended object stretch it radially and squeeze it laterally through this differential effect.
This theorem says point charges cannot be held in stable static equilibrium using electrostatic forces alone.
Electromagnetic energy density divided by light speed squared and multiplied by propagation velocity gives this field quantity per unit volume.
Photons transfer momentum on absorption or reflection, exerting this force per unit area.
This tensor packages electromagnetic tensions and pressures so forces can be found from momentum flux through a surface.
column6: What is the Maxwell stress tensor?

column5: A charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field traces a circle at a frequency independent of speed in the nonrelativistic limit.
A conductor moving across magnetic field lines develops this voltage because charges experience magnetic deflection.
Loops of induced current in a bulk conductor oppose changing magnetic flux and can provide magnetic braking.
A motor's rotating coil generates a voltage opposing the supply, limiting current once the rotor speeds up.
Alternating current crowds toward a conductor's surface increasingly at high frequency through this effect.
A magnet can levitate above a superconductor because expelled magnetic flux creates this perfect diamagnetic response.
This partial differential equation recasts classical dynamics in terms of a principal function whose gradients give canonical momenta.
For integrable periodic systems, these canonical variables pair conserved loop integrals with steadily advancing phases.
A quantity such as a slowly varying oscillator's energy divided by frequency stays nearly constant and is called this.
In the circular restricted three-body problem, an energy-like conserved quantity in the rotating frame bears this name.
A smaller body's gravitational dominance against a massive primary extends roughly to this radius, important for satellite stability.
Only inverse-square and isotropic harmonic central potentials make every bound orbit closed, according to this theorem.
Most invariant tori of a slightly perturbed integrable Hamiltonian survive when their frequencies are sufficiently irrational under this theorem.
A viscous-free potential flow predicts no drag on a body despite everyday experience, a contradiction named for this mechanician.
In inviscid barotropic flow with conservative body forces, circulation around a material loop remains constant under this theorem.
This framework converts a conservation law for a moving system into one for a fixed control volume.
